title: These 6 Modern Collector Cars Aren’t Keeping Up with Inflation

body_markdown:
For the last six years, one buzzword—inflation—has been on everybody’s lips, from Fed Chairs to moms wondering why a gallon of milk costs $4. At the same time, car people have been watching the values of our favorite vehicles climb. Indeed, just about everything with four wheels and an engine has gotten more expensive since 2020, but this didn’t happen simply because of inflation; it’s also thanks to changing market conditions, shifting tastes, and new enthusiasts entering the hobby.


And not all cars appreciated at the same rate, or at the same time. Some barely appreciated at all. Others grew by amounts that look impressive at first glance, but over the longer term haven’t kept up with the rate of inflation of the U.S. dollar. Which, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, was about 29% from January 2020 to July 2026. This means that something that cost $10,000 in 2020 now costs $12,900. If a car went from $10,000 to $12,500 in that time, that means it’s actually gone down in value in real terms. Below are some examples of this trend among modern, post-1990 performance cars, measured by the average increase in condition #2 (excellent) value in our price guide since January 2020.


## [2009–15 Cadillac CTS-V (Sedan and Coupe)](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=cadillac+cts-v)


Martin Klimek/Cadillac


**+14–15%**


The second generation CTS-V was arguably the most exciting new Cadillac in decades, but not thanks to clever luxury tech or dramatic styling like Cadillacs of old. No, this was a serious performer, capable of taking on the super sedans from the German Big Three. The star of the “V” package was the 6.2-liter supercharged LSA V-8, based on the LS9 V-8 from the contemporary[ZR1 Corvette](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/chevrolet/corvette/2009/2009-chevrolet-corvette-zr1?id=aCn1I000000DTM8SAO) , rated at 556 hp/551 lb-ft. and available with either a Tremec six-speed manual or six-speed automatic with paddle shifters. It also came with MagneRide and Brembo brakes. The “Corvette in a fancy suit” quips came immediately.


While the first-generation CTS-V (2004–07) was only available as a sedan, the second-gen car came in sedan, coupe, and wagon forms. The wagon in particular is an enthusiast darling these days, as any fast five-door with a stick-shift is bound to become, and the #2 condition for one is $88,000 (+42% since January 2020), with #1 (concours, or best in the world) condition cars stretching a little past $100K. The sedans and coupes have appreciated at a slower clip, however, and their #3 (good) values are actually flat over the last six years in pure dollar terms. But when you adjust for inflation, prices for cleaner cars are down, too. For example, the #2 value for a sedan is $48,900 and up 14%. In early 2020, that number was $43,000, and adjusted for inflation, that would be over $55K in 2026.


## [2005–12 Porsche Boxster](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=2006+porsche+boxster)


Porsche


**+16**


Porsches tend to be pretty pricey, now more than ever. A clapped-out 911 SC can be a $40,000 car, and new 992s either barely depreciate or don’t depreciate at all, so there are few ways into P-car ownership that make much financial sense. That said, the 987, aka the second-gen Boxster, is *technically* getting a little cheaper.


Most Boxsters of this era came in base, sportier S, or bare-bones Spyder trims. Condition #2 values since 2020 are up from 5% to 12% for base cars, 18% for Boxster S, and 27% for Boxster Spyder, and they range from $26,000 for an early base model 987.1 to $90,000 for a Boxster Spyder. But in inflation-adjusted terms, all of these are under where they were at the start of the decade. For further proof that the Porsche world prefers a fixed roof, we can look to the coupe version of the 987 platform—the[Cayman](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/cayman/2010/2010-porsche-cayman-base?id=aCn1I000000D08aSAC) . All versions of that car are up at least 30% over the same period.


## [2004–16 Aston Martin DB9](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=aston+martin+db9)


Broad Arrow


**+24%**


One of the fastest ways to burn a few thousand dollars is to go to an Aston Martin dealership, buy a new DB-something, and drive it off the lot. Aston is among the quickest-depreciating new car brands out there, to the point where used ones start looking like tempting (but expensive to maintain) deals to enthusiasts of more modest means. Looking at a graph of DB9 values, it appears as if the handsome grand tourer of the 2000s was bucking the trend. Alas, not quite.


From early 2020 to late 2022, DB9 values shot up by over 20%, but since then they have been mostly flat, even as other modern European performance cars with 12-cylinder engines and a fancy badge have been on a tear. The lowest the DB9’s median #2 value ever got was $44,000 in 2020. That would be over $57,000 when adjusted for inflation, but the DB9’s median #2 value today is under $56K. The #2 value ranges from just over $50K for early coupes to a little over $100K for the Volante (convertible) model.


## [2009 Pontiac G8 GXP](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/search?q=pontiac+g8)


GM


**+14%**


While never the flashiest thing on the road, the Pontiac G8 GXP was a super sedan with a 6.2-liter LS3 engine driving the rear wheels. The LS3 was enough to push the G8 (based on an Australian Holden platform) towards 180 mph, and with an optional six-speed manual gearbox it could reel off zero-to-60 mph in 4.7 seconds. Even after Pontiac was dead, the concept came back to life as the[Chevrolet SS](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/chevrolet/ss/2016/2016-chevrolet-ss-base?id=aCn1I000000DWeSSAW) sedan, built between 2014–17.


Pontiac went out with a bang thanks to the GXP, but the market for it remains somewhat ho-hum compared to models from deeper in the brand’s back catalogue. Values have been a bit up and down, peaking at $40,400 for #2 condition in 2022 and dropping a bit since to a current value of $39,200. In January 2020, that number was $34,500, which is roughly $44,700 when adjusted for inflation to today’s dollars.


## [1991–93 BMW M5 (E34)](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/bmw/m5/1991/1991-bmw-m5-base?id=aCn1I000000Csa6SAC)


BMW


**+28%**


The second-generation M5 rode on the E34 platform, and it featured chassis improvements over the base 5-series like different dampers, springs, and thicker anti-roll bars, all fitted by hand as they had been with the car’s[E28](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/bmw/m5/1988/1988-bmw-m5-base?id=aCn1I000000DUukSAG) -based predecessor. The 3.5-liter twin-cam straight-six delivered 310 silky-smooth horsepower and was good enough for 155 mph. Although the Bavarians built the E34 M5 in both sedan and Touring (wagon) forms, only the sedan made it to our shores, and fewer than 1700 examples sold in the U.S. and Canada.


Collector interest has certainly come for the E34 M5, and from 2013 to ’23 the #2 value essentially quadrupled. But from early 2020 to today, the appreciation has slowed down to barely less than the rate of inflation, going from $41,600 (which is a little over $53,800 adjusted for inflation) to $53,300.


## [1990–97 Mazda Miata](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/mazda/mx~5_miata/1991/1991-mazda-mx~5_miata-base?id=aCn1I000000DREPSA4)


James Lipman


**+24%**


The days of the truly cheap NA (1990–97) Miata are long over. A decade ago, picking up a really clean one for four figures was easy peasy, but starting in 2018, increased demand for a diminished supply of these smiley-faced sports cars saw prices jump quickly. Today, the condition #2 value is more than double what it was nine years ago. NA values have grown during this decade, too, and a car in #2 condition is worth roughly $19,000, but that’s under what the inflation-adjusted value was in 2020.


For reference, the NA’s successor—the 1999—2005 NB Miata—has experienced a similar level of appreciation, but lagged behind in general.[NB](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/mazda/mx~5_miata/2000/2000-mazda-mx~5_miata-base?id=aCn1I000000DSFZSA4) values are up over 50% since early 2020.
